For reactions combined algebraically, ΔG° values add up: ΔG° = –nFE°. Hence, when equations are added

Given:
Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe ; E1° = –0.441 V
Fe3+ + e– → Fe2+ ; E2° = +0.771 V
For Fe + 2Fe3+ → 3Fe2+,
2(Fe3+ + e– → Fe2+) – (Fe2+ + 2e– → Fe) gives required equation.
⇒ 2ΔG2° – ΔG1° = ΔG3°
⇒ 2(–FE2°) – (–2FE1°) = –2FE3°
⇒ E3° = E2° – E1° = 0.771 – (–0.441) = 1.212 V

Ps​ = Xsolvent ​× P 
where Xsolvent​ is the mole fraction of the solvent and P is the vapour pressure of the pure solvent. 
The mole fraction of the solvent is Xsolvent ​= N/(n+N)​, where N is the number of moles of the solvent and n is the number of moles of the solute. 
So, Ps​=[N/(n+N)] ​× P. 
Rearranging this equation to find the relative lowering of vapor pressure: 
(P−Ps)/P​​=1−Ps/P​​=1−N/(n+N​)=(n+N−N)/(n+N) ​=n/n+N
(P−Ps)/P​​​=n/n+N

"Explanation: Identify the plant with conjoint, collateral, and open vascular bundles.
Concept: Plant Anatomy.
Solution: A conjoint vascular bundle has xylem and phloem on the same radius. Collateral means the phloem is on the outer side and the xylem is on the inner side. Open refers to the presence of a cambium layer between the xylem and phloem, allowing for secondary growth. This arrangement is a characteristic feature of dicot stems. Among the options, the sunflower is a dicot, while the others (sugarcane, maize, and wheat) are monocots.
Final Answer: Sunflower."
